c1.label: Q1
c1.prompt: `pick random -100 to 100` gives you a number. What decides which one?

A.text: The program picks the middle one

B.text: The micro:bit picks one you cannot predict

C.text: It counts up from -100 every time

c1.why: That is what random means — a number you cannot work out ahead of time, chosen fresh each time the block runs.

c2.label: Q2
c2.prompt: You run the same random program twice and the car takes a different path each time. Is the program different?

B.text: No — the program is identical; only the numbers differ

C.text: No — the paths are the same and it just looks different

c2.why: The blocks never change. What changes is the number the random block hands over each time it runs.

c3.label: Q3
c3.prompt: A wheel speed of -100 means what?

A.text: The wheel turns backwards at full speed

c3.why: The minus sign is direction, not size. -100 is as fast as 100 — the other way.

r1.label: Q1

B.text: Picks one speed at the start and keeps it

C.text: Drives straight at a random speed

D.text: Wanders — direction and speed keep changing

r1.why: Both wheels get their own new number every trip round the loop, so the car changes what it is doing constantly.

r2.label: Q2
r2.prompt: How is this different from giving each wheel its own random number?

D.text: Both wheels always match, so it never curves

r2.why: One number for both wheels means no speed difference — and no speed difference means no turn. It runs forward and back in a line.

r3.label: Q3
r3.prompt: What can this car never do?
r3.why: The range starts at 0, so no negative number can ever come out — and negative is what reversing needs.

r4.label: Q4
r4.prompt: There is no `forever` here. What does the car do?

D.text: Picks one pair of speeds and keeps them

r4.why: The random blocks run once at start-up. One pair of numbers goes to the motors and stays there.

d1.label: Q1
d1.prompt: The car only ever runs in a straight line, forwards or backwards. Which change fixes it?

B.text: The motor block should use `right_speed` for the right wheel

d1.why: The right variable is filled in but never used — both wheels get the left number, so they always match.

d2.label: Q2
d2.prompt: The car sits completely still. What is missing?

B.text: The random blocks that fill the variables

d2.why: Both variables still hold 0, and 0 to both wheels is "stopped". The numbers have to be put in before they can come out.

b1.label: Q1
b1.prompt: Starting from the top of `forever`, put these in order: 1 send both numbers to the motors · 2 pick a random left speed · 3 pick a random right speed
b1.why: Fill both boxes first, then hand them over together. Driving between the two picks would use one new number and one old one.

b2.label: Q2
b2.prompt: You want the car to wander but never reverse. Which range should the random blocks use?
b2.why: Cutting the negatives out of the range removes reverse. The car can still turn, because the two wheels still differ.
